statement: A test that pins a hash over output containing a git commit sha is only as reproducible as the commit, and a commit made under the developer's own git config is not reproducible: with commit.gpgsign=true the commit object carries a gpgsig block from that machine's key, so the sha — and every pin derived from it — differs per host. cejel's v17/v22 byte-stability guard failed on a macOS host and a Linux container from origin/main with different hashes on each, and passed only on CI, which has no signing key, while its own comment claimed the fixture was reproducible across machines. Make fixture git hermetic: mask global and system config, pass identity and dates through the environment, commit with --no-gpg-sign, and assert the fixture commit sha by name before any output pin, so environmental drift fails as "fixture not reproducible" instead of as a scan-output change. A guard red on every developer machine and green only on CI guards nothing a developer can see.
